_doc: KIRSTEN dating cabinet (#39, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #45). Seattle's metal-system pipe (Prof. Frederick Kirsten, Boeing wind-tunnel engineer, designed 1936). THE GENERATION SYSTEM (Dave Whitney's collector classification, on pipedia): Gen 1 1936-1958 (no O-rings, precise machining) / Gen 1.5 transition mid-late-50s (mixed parts) / Gen 2 1958-1985 (O-rings both ends; 1958 = incorporation, 'biggest change' per Lynn Kirsten) / Gen 3 1985+. PATENT-STAMP LADDER: 'PAT APPLIED FOR' = 1936-1938 ONLY (tightest cliff). Factory kept NO records (Lynn Kirsten confirmed) -> generation edges approx. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Kirsten_Pipe_Company.json (Whitney).

history_anchors._doc: 1936: Frederick Kirsten designs the pipe (physician told him to quit smoking; the radiator-valve system traps tars/moisture). 5-6 components: mouthpiece, radiator body, valve, bowl, bowl screw (+bowl ring). Gene Kirsten ran the factory for years. 1958: company INCORPORATED = the big model/technique change (Gen 2, O-rings). EARLY BOWLS WERE MADE BY KAYWOODIE (unstamped!); Kirsten-made bowls stamped on the bottom (start date unclear); bowl adapters arrive ~transition period. 1960s: 'Eternalum' antiqued brass-tone finish ('Traditional'); cigarette holders in the 50s-60s (3 sizes). Corncob bowls exist (probably Missouri-made); one Doodler bowl mated to a Kirsten known (pre-1964, Mincer link!). Finishes: polished silver/gold/black, rough 'Heritage' Parkerized. 1976-77 catalog mirrored on pipedia.
history_anchors.generation_models: Gen 1 straights: Companion (rough 1st ed.), S Standard (full-length fins), M Medium, L Large, A ARISTOCRAT (XL). Gen 1.5: K Companion, M, L + oddballs (Thrifty w/ reverse black valve, No-Letter short pipe). Gen 2: K Companion, G Gem, S Sportsman, SX, M Mariner, MB, L Lancer; quarter-bents A Aladdin, V Vagabond, CX Cavalier, T Tyrolean; full-bents W Westerner, B Beau Geste, P Premier, F Firesider. Gen 3: JX Jewel, M Mariner, L Lancer; RX Regent, H Horizon; EX Esquire, DX Designer. X suffix = brass-tone, B = black.

brand_marks.physical: Kirsten script logo on the radiator body (shield logo ONLY on the 'Thrifty'; early Companions sometimes unmarked). Model letter stamps (S/M/L/A...). O-rings: none = Gen 1; one end only = Gen 1.5; both = Gen 2/3.

line_years._notes: Model->generation mapping per Whitney's table; generation edges approx (1958 incorporation is the firm one; 1985 Gen2/3 edge 'with possibly some backward overlap'). Models SPANNING generations NOT encoded: Companion (1+1.5+2), Standard/Medium/Large letters, Mariner + Lancer (2+3), Sportsman/Aladdin/Cavalier/Premier (single-gen but common-word collision risk accepted-out). 'Thrifty' = transition oddball ~mid-50s -> note only.

table.label: 'PAT APPLIED FOR' stamp = first ~2 years only (1936-1938) — the tightest Kirsten cliff
'PATS & PATS PENDING' = ~1938-1958 (Gen 1 tail; hypothetical end edge per Whitney)
O-rings on valve + mouthpiece = Gen 2/3 (1958+); one-end-only = the mid-50s transition

channels_future.kaywoodie_bowls: Early unstamped Kirsten bowls = Kaywoodie-made (cross-cabinet fact; bowls alone are NOT attributable).
channels_future.catalog_1976: The mirrored 1976-77 catalog page -> Gen 2 model roster verification.
channels_future.serial_less: No serials/records exist (factory-confirmed) — generations are the ceiling of precision.
